Topic 4.2: Modeling using slab technique

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Modeling using slab technique. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you model?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Model freely for fun plasticine/ paper machier, for

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MODELING USING SLAB TECHNIQUE
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Modeling using slab technique helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: MODELING USING SLAB TECHNIQUE

PART 1: Model freely for fun plasticine/ paper machier, for

What this means
In this part you learn to Model freely for fun plasticine/ paper machier, for. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Model freely for fun plasticine/ paper machier, for.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Modeling using slab technique” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Model freely for fun plasticine/ paper machier, for. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Modeling using slab technique is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Modeling using slab technique” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: Model freely for fun plasticine/ paper machier, for)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Modeling using slab technique to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Model freely for fun plasticine/ paper machier, for.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Modeling using slab technique from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Modeling using slab technique: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Modeling using slab technique?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you model?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Modeling using slab technique means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Model freely for fun plasticine/ paper machier, for.
